remediation.title: What happens if we waste things?

questions.question: Sana wants to find out how learners in her class travel to school. What should she do first?
questions.options: Tell everyone the answer she expects | Draw a chart of the results | Decide the question she wants to answer | Choose the colours for her poster
questions.correctAnswer: Decide the question she wants to answer
questions.explanation: Every piece of research starts with a clear question. Once Sana knows exactly what she wants to find out, all the other steps become easier.

questions.question: Amina asks every learner in her class the same question: how many brothers and sisters do you have? What kind of question is she asking?
questions.options: A guess | An opinion | An open question | A number question
questions.correctAnswer: A number question
questions.explanation: The answer is a number, so it is a number question. Number questions are easy to count up and put in a chart.

questions.question: Sana has collected twenty answers to her questionnaire. What is the best next step, so that a pattern can show?
questions.options: Throw away the answers she did not expect | Record the results in a pictogram | Start again with a new question | Ask twenty more people the same question
questions.correctAnswer: Record the results in a pictogram
questions.explanation: Recording results in a pictogram lets a pattern show at a glance. Throwing away surprising answers would spoil the research.

questions.question: Which list shows the steps of an investigation in the best order?
questions.options: Collect answers, ask a question, say what you found, record the results | Ask a question, collect answers, record the results, say what you found | Record the results, ask a question, collect answers, say what you found | Say what you found, record the results, collect answers, ask a question
questions.correctAnswer: Ask a question, collect answers, record the results, say what you found
questions.explanation: An investigation works best in order: first the question, then collecting answers, then recording them, and finally saying what you found out.

questions.question: Rami is analysing the topic of chocolate. His mother says chocolate should be a treat for special days, because too much sugar is bad for teeth. What has Rami found?
questions.options: A pictogram | A shared goal | A number question | A perspective with a reason
questions.correctAnswer: A perspective with a reason
questions.explanation: A perspective is a way of seeing a topic. His mother gives her point of view and the reason behind it — exactly what an analyst listens for.

questions.question: A chart shows that 12 learners like football, 5 like reading and 3 like drawing. Which sentence says what the data shows?
questions.options: The chart proves drawing is boring | Learners who like football are the cleverest | Most learners in the chart chose football | Reading is the best hobby for everyone
questions.correctAnswer: Most learners in the chart chose football
questions.explanation: Saying what the data shows means describing the numbers, not adding your own opinion. The biggest number in this chart is football, with 12.

questions.question: Rami asks learners, teachers and parents about games at break time, and each group says something different. What does this show him?
questions.options: Only one of the groups is telling the truth | One topic can have many different perspectives | The topic is too hard to analyse | He should only listen to the adults
questions.correctAnswer: One topic can have many different perspectives
questions.explanation: On most topics, different people see things differently. A good analyst collects those different perspectives instead of picking just one.

questions.question: Rami notices that when learners leave the taps running, the school runs short of water. Which is a sensible first idea to help?
questions.options: Make a friendly sign reminding everyone to turn the taps off | Stop everyone from using water at school | Ignore it, because he did not cause the problem | Wait and hope somebody else fixes it
questions.correctAnswer: Make a friendly sign reminding everyone to turn the taps off
questions.explanation: Analysis is not only about looking — it is also about doing. A small, sensible action like a reminder sign can change what people do every day.

questions.question: Which of these is a factual claim — something you could check?
questions.options: Mango juice is nicer than orange juice | Rainy days feel boring | Break time is the best part of the day | Our school has twelve classrooms
questions.correctAnswer: Our school has twelve classrooms
questions.explanation: A factual claim can be checked — you could walk round the school and count the classrooms. The other three are opinions about what people like or feel.

questions.question: Nadia’s research question is: what does a healthy lunch cost? Which source is most likely to be relevant?
questions.options: A song about the sea | A price list from the local market | A poster about road safety | A storybook about a dragon
questions.correctAnswer: A price list from the local market
questions.explanation: A relevant source is one that really helps with your question. A market price list tells Nadia what food costs — the others are about different topics.

questions.question: Nadia finds an advert made by a sweet company. It says sweets make a great lunch. Why should she be careful with this source?
questions.options: Adverts are always true | A sweet company knows the most about healthy lunches | The company wants to sell sweets, so its advice may not be fair | Adverts are checked by teachers before they are shown
questions.correctAnswer: The company wants to sell sweets, so its advice may not be fair
questions.explanation: A good evaluator always asks who made a source and why. The company earns money when people buy sweets, so its advert may not give fair advice about lunch.

questions.question: After a team project, Yusuf thinks back over his work. Which sentence shows real reflection about his part in the team?
questions.options: It was fun and then we went home | I drew the chart well, and next time I will also help ask the questions | We did the project and now it is finished | I cannot remember anything about it
questions.correctAnswer: I drew the chart well, and next time I will also help ask the questions
questions.explanation: Real reflection is deeper than saying it was fun. Yusuf names his contribution, and says what he will improve next time.

questions.question: Yusuf has just learned to make a tally chart. What is the best way for him to reflect on his learning?
questions.options: List everything his team did wrong | Say what he learned and what helped him learn it | Say the whole project was easy | Copy a friend’s reflection into his book
questions.correctAnswer: Say what he learned and what helped him learn it
questions.explanation: Good reflection on learning has two parts: what you actually learned, and what helped you learn it — so you can use that help again.

questions.question: Yusuf’s team finished their poster on time, but two members did almost all of the work. What would a good reflection on the teamwork say?
questions.options: We finished on time, but we did not share the jobs fairly | Nothing about our teamwork went well | The poster should have been bigger | Everything about our teamwork was perfect
questions.correctAnswer: We finished on time, but we did not share the jobs fairly
questions.explanation: A good reflection names both a strength and a limitation. Finishing on time went well; sharing the jobs fairly is what the team could do better.

questions.question: Layla’s team is starting a project about healthy diets. What should the team agree on first?
questions.options: Their shared goal | Who will win at the end | Which snack to bring | Who is the fastest writer
questions.correctAnswer: Their shared goal
questions.explanation: Every strong team begins by agreeing its shared goal — the one result everyone is working for. Then all the jobs can point the same way.

questions.question: Layla’s team cannot agree which survey question to ask. What is the fairest way to decide?
questions.options: Each person secretly does their own idea | Let the loudest person choose | Talk about the choices, then take a vote | Give up on the project
questions.correctAnswer: Talk about the choices, then take a vote
questions.explanation: Teams often disagree, and that is normal. Talking it through and voting lets everyone have a say, so the team can move on together.

questions.question: The team must present its findings. Hodan is great at drawing and Bilal speaks very clearly. How should they share the jobs?
questions.options: They should swap jobs every minute | One person should do everything | Bilal draws the poster and Hodan gives the talk | Hodan draws the poster and Bilal gives the talk
questions.correctAnswer: Hodan draws the poster and Bilal gives the talk
questions.explanation: The clever trick is to match each job to a person’s skill. Then every job is done by someone who does it well, and the whole team shines.

questions.question: Idris is planning a short talk about keeping the beach clean. What will best help his talk stay clear and not wander?
questions.options: Speaking as fast as he can | Adding every fact he has ever learned | Whispering so nobody hears his mistakes | A skeleton plan with a beginning, a middle and an end
questions.correctAnswer: A skeleton plan with a beginning, a middle and an end
questions.explanation: A skeleton plan is a simple frame that holds a talk up. With a beginning, a middle and an end, Idris always knows what comes next.

questions.question: While Amina presents her project, what should a really good listener in the audience do?
questions.options: Pay full attention, then ask a sensible question at the end | Look out of the window until it is time to clap | Interrupt her with a better idea | Chat quietly with a friend
questions.correctAnswer: Pay full attention, then ask a sensible question at the end
questions.explanation: A great communicator is a great listener. Paying full attention and asking a thoughtful question shows Amina that her ideas were really heard.

questions.question: A team is building a model bridge together. What makes the team work best?
questions.options: One person builds while the others watch | Everyone has a job that helps the team | Working with no plan and no talking | Keeping your best ideas secret
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone has a job that helps the team
questions.explanation: A good team shares the work. When every member has a helpful job, the bridge gets built faster and everyone feels proud of it.

questions.question: The team wants to know which bridge design their classmates like best. What could they do?
questions.options: Guess what everyone probably thinks | Ask one friend and stop there | Choose a design without asking anyone | Ask each classmate and count the answers with a tally
questions.correctAnswer: Ask each classmate and count the answers with a tally
questions.explanation: A little survey is a fair way to find out what people think. Asking everyone and keeping a tally shows which design is really the favourite.

questions.question: Imagine a new rule that says only tall children may use the library. What is the best way to describe this rule?
questions.options: Fair, because tall children read more | Not fair, because it leaves people out for no good reason | Fair, because rules are always fair | It is not really a rule at all
questions.correctAnswer: Not fair, because it leaves people out for no good reason
questions.explanation: A rule detective asks whether a rule treats people fairly. Being tall has nothing to do with reading, so this rule shuts children out for no good reason.

questions.question: Warda wants to find out why her school has a no-running rule in the corridor. Who would be the best person to ask?
questions.options: Nobody — she should just guess | Someone who has never visited her school | A learner at a school far away | A teacher who helps make the school rules
questions.correctAnswer: A teacher who helps make the school rules
questions.explanation: Good researchers ask the people who really know. A teacher who helps make the rules can explain exactly why the rule is there.

questions.question: Khadija is going to interview her grandmother about life long ago. Which is the best question to prepare?
questions.options: What was school like when you were my age? | How old are you exactly? | Do you know what I did at school today? | Can I go out to play now?
questions.correctAnswer: What was school like when you were my age?
questions.explanation: The best interview questions invite a story. Asking about school long ago lets her grandmother share memories that Khadija could never find out another way.

questions.question: Two friends disagree. Sahra thinks buying fair-trade bananas helps farmers, and Liban is not so sure. What should they do next?
questions.options: Stop being friends | Decide that both of them must be wrong | Listen to each other’s reasons and find out more together | Agree with whoever talks loudest
questions.correctAnswer: Listen to each other’s reasons and find out more together
questions.explanation: Friends can have two different ideas and still work together. Listening to each other’s reasons — and finding out more — is how good thinkers handle a disagreement.

questions.question: A new learner joins the class and does not know anybody yet. Which action would help her feel welcome?
questions.options: Say hello, learn her name and invite her to join your game | Wait a few weeks before speaking to her | Point at her and whisper with your friends | Let her sit alone so she can settle in
questions.correctAnswer: Say hello, learn her name and invite her to join your game
questions.explanation: Think how you would feel on your first day. A warm hello, hearing your name and being invited to play are the things that make a new person feel they belong.

questions.question: Asha wants to learn how her family makes bread. What should she do?
questions.options: Ask a family member to show her, and watch carefully | Never ask anyone about it | Guess and hope for the best | Wait until she is grown up
questions.correctAnswer: Ask a family member to show her, and watch carefully
questions.explanation: Families can teach us so much. Asking and watching carefully is one of the very first ways we find things out.

questions.question: Deeqa says girls cannot be builders. What is the best reply?
questions.options: She is right, some jobs are only for boys | Girls and boys can both learn the skills to do any job | Only grown-ups are allowed to talk about jobs | Builders are not a real job
questions.correctAnswer: Girls and boys can both learn the skills to do any job
questions.explanation: When we hear a claim, we can stop and ask if it is really true. Girls and boys can learn to do any job — doctors, builders, pilots and more.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What do we know about jobs?

questions.question: Which of these actions helps to save water at home?
questions.options: Leaving the tap running all day | Watering the path instead of the plants | Turning off the tap while you brush your teeth | Filling buckets and pouring them away
questions.correctAnswer: Turning off the tap while you brush your teeth
questions.explanation: Sorting actions into save or waste helps us choose well. Turning the tap off while you brush saves clean water; the other actions waste it.

questions.question: Zahra wants to know which country her rice comes from. Where could she look first?
questions.options: Nowhere — it is impossible to find out | The label on the rice packet | Under her bed | In a storybook about space
questions.correctAnswer: The label on the rice packet
questions.explanation: Labels are a handy source of information. Reading the packet is a quick, clever way to start finding out where food comes from.

questions.question: The class wants to learn how to recycle plastic. Which source would help them most?
questions.options: A recipe for soup | A song about counting | A cartoon about dinosaurs | A poster about recycling from the town clean-up team
questions.correctAnswer: A poster about recycling from the town clean-up team
questions.explanation: A helpful source is about your question. The clean-up team’s recycling poster is exactly on topic — the others are about something else.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What happens if we waste things?

questions.question: Faisal asked his classmates their favourite way to be active, and now he wants to share what he found. What could he do?
questions.options: Say his own favourite is the winner | Tell the class what most people chose | Lose the answers and say nothing | Keep all the answers secret
questions.correctAnswer: Tell the class what most people chose
questions.explanation: Sharing what you found is part of every survey. Telling the class what most people chose lets everyone learn from Faisal’s finding-out.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: How can we be active and healthy?
